core_obligations: Reduce part (1) to part (2): for a closed Z with D intersect Z an effective Cartier divisor, put F equal to the structure sheaf of Z, note that the Cartier condition is equivalent to injectivity of multiplication by the section on F, and identify the two cycle classes with those of F and of the restriction of F, so that part (1) follows from part (2) (proof lines 5192-5199).

Set up part (2): write the cycle class of F as a positive combination of integral closed subschemes W_j of delta-dimension k + 1, observe that injectivity of multiplication by the section forces each W_j to be contained in the complement of D, and by definition of the Gysin pullback write i^* of the class as the sum of the classes of the intersections D intersect W_j (proof lines 5201-5210).

Compare coefficients: for an integral closed Z of dimension k with generic point xi, let A be the local ring there, M the stalk of F and f a local equation for D, so that the support of M has dimension one, multiplication by f is injective and the length of M/fM is finite; that length is the coefficient of Z in the pullback of the sheaf class, while the sum over the minimal primes in the support of M of the local length times the order of f is the coefficient of Z in the sum of the cycles of the intersections; the equality follows from additivity of divisors for the restricted family (proof lines 5211-5233).
proof_roadmap: Reduce the subscheme statement to the sheaf statement (proof lines 5192-5199).
Write the class of the sheaf through its components and use injectivity of the section to keep them off the divisor (proof lines 5201-5210).
Compare coefficients in the local ring and invoke additivity of divisors (proof lines 5211-5233).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the Gysin pullback in two basic situations: the class of a closed subscheme whose intersection with the divisor is again a Cartier divisor, and the class of a coherent sheaf on which multiplication by the defining section is injective (statement lines 5169-5189, tag 02TB). The first part is reduced to the second through the identification of cycle classes of subschemes and structure sheaves, and the second requires a coefficient comparison in a one-dimensional local module where the length of the quotient by the local equation must be matched against a sum over the minimal primes weighted by orders, which is exactly the additivity statement for restricted divisors. That coefficient comparison is the substance, so the claim is H2.
